implementation_notes: Kotlin inherits the Java layers and adds its own: Koin and Hilt both on the classpath, kotlinx.serialization and Jackson both configured, java.time and ThreeTenABP both in use. Each coexistence is a small compile-time decision with no error, and the resulting configuration surface is the sum of all of them. The detection is the dependency report plus a grep; the completion mechanism is a Gradle resolution strategy or an architecture test that fails the build when both symbols are referenced, which is a genuinely Java/Kotlin-shaped answer.
idiom_name: two DI frameworks, two serialisers, two date libraries
pitfalls: Two DI frameworks both scanning the same package double-registers beans and fails at startup in a way that suggests a different problem.
`kotlinx.serialization` and Jackson on the same types means two annotations on one class and two reflection paths.
Java-interop annotations on a Kotlin-only codebase are a migration residue that is easy to keep and hard to remove.
